deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (inferred by me, not stated on the page). The page belongs to Riemann's heat-conduction material connected with the 1858/61 Paris prize question on stationary isothermal families. Read with the side computations, the page appears to study a potential (temperature) u(x,y,z) with gradient (p,q,r)=grad u. The key assumptions are:
- Laplace's equation, written as the divergence condition C: p_x+q_y+r_z=0.
- u is a function of m=|grad u|^2 alone. This is a Lamé-type isothermal / isoparametric condition.
The cases are sorted by how many independent quantities (p,q,r) depend on. This page treats the rank-2 case (p,q,r depend on two variables) and then the rank-1 case.

(1) Rank-2 case. The image is a surface in (p,q,r)-space, so write r=r(p,q) with a=r_p, b=r_q, i.e. r=ap+bq. Differentiating r=ap+bq and using dr=a dp+b dq gives p da+q db=0, i.e.
- p a_p+q b_p=0 and p a_q+q b_q=0 (this is Euler's relation: r is homogeneous of degree 1, so the surface is a cone);
- hence the determinant vanishes: a_p b_q-a_q b_p=0.

(2) Legendre transform (my reading of 'aequatio (5)'). Set s=u-px-qy-rz. Then ds=-x dp-y dq-z dr=-(x+az)dp-(y+bz)dq, so s=s(p,q) and
 s_p=-x-az, s_q=-y-bz   (II).

(3) Change of variables. Take (p,q,z) as independent variables, with Jacobian J=x_p y_q-x_q y_p. Then:
- p_x=y_q/J and q_y=x_p/J;
- p_z=(x_q y_z-x_z y_q)/J and q_z=(x_z y_p-x_p y_z)/J;
- r_z=a p_z+b q_z.
Multiplying the divergence condition by J gives
 x_p+y_q-a(y_q x_z-x_q y_z)-b(x_p y_z-y_p x_z)=0,
exactly as Riemann writes.

(4) Substitution. From (II): x_p=-z a_p-s_pp, x_q=-z a_q-s_pq, y_p=-z b_p-s_pq, y_q=-z b_q-s_qq, x_z=-a, y_z=-b. The equation becomes
 z[(1+b^2)a_p-ab(a_q+b_p)+(1+a^2)b_q]+(1+b^2)s_pp-2ab s_pq+(1+a^2)s_qq=0.
Riemann writes +2ab in the s-part; that sign is a slip.

(5) Splitting. a, b and s do not depend on z, so the z-coefficient vanishes separately:
 (1+r_q^2)r_pp-2r_p r_q r_pq+(1+r_p^2)r_qq=0.
This is the minimal-surface equation for the graph r(p,q). By (1) the Gaussian-curvature numerator r_pp r_qq-r_pq^2 also vanishes. A surface with H=K=0 is a plane, so a and b are constant. Rotating axes gives r=0, and the s-part becomes s_pp+s_qq=0. (This also follows because the Hessian of s is minus the inverse Hessian of a harmonic u(x,y).)

(6) Imposing u=Phi(m), m=p^2+q^2 (side computation). We have u=s-p s_p-q s_q. Write s=psi(m)+t; then u=psi+t-2m psi'-(p t_p+q t_q). This splits into:
- psi-2m psi'=function of m;
- p t_p+q t_q=t, i.e. t=p chi(rho) with rho=q/p.
So s=psi(m)+p chi(q/p). Then:
- -x=s_p=2p psi'+chi-rho chi';
- -y=s_q=2q psi'+chi';
- s_pp=4p^2 psi''+2psi'+(rho^2/p)chi'' and s_qq=4q^2 psi''+2psi'+(1/p)chi''.
The Laplace equation gives 4m psi''+4psi'+(1+rho^2)chi''/p=0. Using p=sqrt(m)/sqrt(1+rho^2), this is
 sqrt(m)(4psi'+4m psi'')+(1+rho^2)^(3/2) chi''=0.
Riemann writes a minus sign here.

(7) Separation of variables. Set sqrt(m)(4psi'+4m psi'')=K, so chi''=K(1+rho^2)^(-3/2) up to the sign. Then:
- chi'=K rho/sqrt(1+rho^2)+b;
- chi=K sqrt(1+rho^2)+a+b rho;
- chi-rho chi'=K/sqrt(1+rho^2)+a.
Therefore
 -(x+a)=(2 sqrt(m) psi'+K)/sqrt(1+rho^2) and -(y+b)=rho(2 sqrt(m) psi'+K)/sqrt(1+rho^2),
and so (x+a)^2+(y+b)^2=(2 sqrt(m) psi'+K)^2, a function of m and hence of u. Conclusion: the isothermal surfaces are coaxial circular cylinders.

(8) Rank-1 case: p,q,r functions of m only. Since u=Phi(m), grad u is parallel to grad m, so psi1:psi2:psi3=m_x:m_y:m_z. Then C=0 gives Sum psi_i' m_{x_i}=0, i.e. Sum psi_i psi_i'=0. But Sum psi_i^2=m gives Sum psi_i psi_i'=1/2. So this case is impossible.
errors: Sign slip in the transformed Laplace equation: the mixed term is -2ab s_pq, not +2ab s_pq. It is harmless, because a=b=0 afterwards.

Sign slip in sqrt(m)(4psi'+4m psi'')-(1+rho^2)^(3/2)chi''=0: the correct sign is +. The side computation likewise has -(1+rho^2)chi'' and omits the factor 1/p (it sets p=1). Taken literally, the sign would make K enter the cylinder radius as 2K+2c/sqrt(m) instead of 2c/sqrt(m). With the correct sign, mpsi'=(K/2)sqrt(m)+c and the radius is R=2c/sqrt(m), i.e. |grad u|~1/R, which is the logarithmic potential. The qualitative conclusion (coaxial cylinders) is unaffected.
x+a=-(2psi'(m)+K)/sqrt(1+rho^2) omits the factor sqrt(m) on psi'. It should read 2 sqrt(m) psi'(m)+K, since p=sqrt(m)/sqrt(1+rho^2).
The text says s is a function of z,p,q; in fact ds has no dz term, so s=s(p,q). This is minor wording.
Step (5): 'minimal plus zero curvature implies plane' is correct, but stated without proof. The vanishing of a_p b_q-a_q b_p supplies K=0, and the z-coefficient supplies H=0.

results.what: Legendre (contact) transformation of a potential with constrained gradient image, used to linearize the problem: s=u-px-qy-rz, s_p=-x-az, s_q=-y-bz
A divergence-free gradient field whose image is a surface forces that surface to be both a cone (homogeneous of degree 1) and a solution of the minimal-surface equation, hence a plane
results.modern_name: Minimal cones in R^3 are planes; a surface with H=K=0 is planar
results.usually_credited_to: classical differential geometry (Lagrange/Meusnier for the minimal-surface equation)

results.what: Classification of harmonic u with u=Phi(|grad u|^2) when grad u has rank 2: the level surfaces are coaxial circular cylinders; rank 1 is impossible (planes need constant gradient)
results.modern_name: Isoparametric (harmonic) functions in R^3: planes, spheres, cylinders (special harmonic case of the Somigliana-Levi-Civita-Segre classification); related to Lamé isothermal families
results.usually_credited_to: Lamé (isothermal families, 1830s); general isoparametric classification Somigliana 1919, Levi-Civita 1937, Segre 1938

results.what: Integration of chi''=K(1+rho^2)^(-3/2) and of 4(m psi')'=K/sqrt(m)

deep.surprise_reason: The methods (Legendre transform, minimal-surface equation, separation of variables) are standard for the period. The notable point is the clean case analysis: rank of grad u, minimal cone implies plane, coaxial cylinders, rank 1 impossible. This classifies harmonic 'isoparametric' temperature fields, a special case of a classification usually attributed to Somigliana, Levi-Civita and Segre (1919-1938). Even so, the harmonic special case with Lamé's isothermal condition was close to known 19th-century material, and the work is tied to Riemann's documented Paris-prize investigations. It is a nice unpublished detail rather than a major priority claim.

chi=K sqrt(1+rho^2)+a+b rho solves chi''=K(1+rho^2)^(-3/2) and gives chi-rho chi'=K/sqrt(1+rho^2)+a (both entries are 0).
General solution gives m psi'=(K/2)sqrt(m)+c, i.e. 2 sqrt(m) psi'=K+2c/sqrt(m). With the corrected sign, the cylinder radius is 2c/sqrt(m) (logarithmic potential).
Consistency check: u=log R is harmonic with |grad u|^2=1/R^2, a function of u. Its isotherms are coaxial cylinders, matching the page's conclusion.
